set_cool_setpoint.description: Set the cooling setpoint (°F); switches to COOL mode.

set_heat_setpoint.description: Set the heating setpoint (°F); switches to HEAT mode.

methods.notes: The module implements a Marvell "WM-DISCOVER" SSDP variant on 239.255.255.250:1900; the reply's Location points at the device. openHAB auto-discovers this way. Confirm a hit with GET /tstat (its shape is unmistakable).

match.description: A Marvell/USNAP thermostat answering WM-DISCOVER; confirm with GET /tstat.

device.name: Radio Thermostat CT30/CT50/CT80 (+ 3M Filtrete 3M50)
device.notes:
The Radio Thermostat CT30/CT50/CT80 (and the 3M Filtrete 3M50 rebrand) are Wi-Fi thermostats with a documented local REST API. The vendor's cloud (my.radiothermostat.com) was discontinued on 2023-05-15 — the page now literally reads "RTCOA - Discontinued" — so the local API is the only thing keeping these units smart. Textbook rescue: plain HTTP, JSON bodies, no authentication.
ENDPOINTS (HTTP port 80, JSON; GET reads, POST writes):
  /tstat            main state: tmode, fmode, temp, tstate, fstate,
                    t_heat/t_cool setpoints, override, hold, time
  /tstat/model      model + firmware string
  /tstat/led        energy_led: 0 off / 1 green / 2 yellow / 4 red
  /tstat/program/<heat|cool>/<mon..sun>   per-day schedule
  /tstat/program/<heat|cool>              whole-week schedule
  /sys, /sys/name, /sys/command (reboot), /sys/mode, network config
  /cloud            POST {"enabled":0} to stop the dead-cloud callbacks
Values: tmode 0 OFF / 1 HEAT / 2 COOL / 3 AUTO; fmode 0 AUTO / 1 AUTO-CIRCULATE / 2 ON; tstate 0/1/2 (OFF/HEAT/COOL); temp is a float °F. time = {day, hour, minute} with day 0 = Monday. Success {"success":0}, errors {"error":-1}; transient values read as -1. The web server is single-threaded (one connection at a time) and does not support chunked encoding.
CAVEAT: t_heat is settable only in HEAT mode (the thermostat auto-switches); AUTO mode and humidity control are CT80-only. Recall the CT80 Rev A/Rev B and CT-30/CT50 feature differences before assuming a field exists.

openness.notes: The API is vendor-documented (Wi-Fi USNAP Module API v1.3), but that PDF is under a restrictive licence that forbids redistribution — so this spec paraphrases the protocol as derived facts rather than reproducing it. Two independent clients (radiotherm, openHAB) confirm the endpoints.

upstream_docs.covers: The /tstat resources, SSDP discovery and the /cloud disable POST; confirms the cloud is defunct.
upstream_docs.title: openHAB — RadioThermostat binding

credentials.notes: The local REST API is unauthenticated on the LAN — anything on the network can read and set the thermostat. Provisioning passes the Wi-Fi passphrase over the module's setup network.

factory_reset.effect: Clears Wi-Fi and schedule configuration, returning the thermostat to setup. Performed from the on-device menu; the exact key sequence is model-specific.

procedures.basis: Documented in the thermostat's own menu / vendor manual; not replayed here.
procedures.name: On-device factory reset

steps.action: Use the thermostat's on-screen menu to factory reset / clear Wi-Fi.
steps.expect: The thermostat returns to Wi-Fi setup.

methods.description: Join the thermostat's setup AP and configure the home Wi-Fi through the module's network-configuration resource; then disable the dead cloud with POST /cloud {"enabled":0}.

steps.action: Set the home Wi-Fi via the module's network configuration resource.
steps.expect: The thermostat joins the LAN and answers GET /tstat.

steps.action: POST /cloud {"enabled":0} to stop the (now dead) cloud callbacks.

setup.notes: Wi-Fi provisioning uses the module's own system/network resources (its setup AP + network configuration). No account is needed. Because the vendor cloud is dead, a newly reset unit should have its cloud callbacks disabled with POST /cloud {"enabled":0}. Provisioning wire steps are not transcribed here.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi can be reconfigured through the module's network resource while the thermostat is reachable.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Endpoints and field semantics are paraphrased from the vendor Wi-Fi USNAP API v1.3 and corroborated by mhrivnak/radiotherm and the openHAB binding.

http_endpoints.description: Current mode/fan/temperature and setpoints. Fields: tmode (0 OFF/1 HEAT/ 2 COOL/3 AUTO), fmode (0 AUTO/1 AUTO-CIRC/2 ON), temp (float °F), tstate (0/1/2), fstate (0/1), t_heat, t_cool, override, hold, time {day,hour,minute}.
http_endpoints.name: Read thermostat state

http_endpoints.description: Accepts a partial object, e.g. {"tmode":1,"t_heat":68} or {"tmode":2, "t_cool":75}. Setting t_heat requires HEAT mode (the thermostat auto-switches). {"hold":1}/{"override":1} pin a temporary setpoint.
http_endpoints.name: Set thermostat state

http_endpoints.description: The model and firmware string — a quick identity check.
http_endpoints.name: Model + firmware

http_endpoints.description: Body {"enabled":0} stops the thermostat contacting the (now dead) Radio Thermostat cloud.
http_endpoints.name: Disable cloud callbacks
